answer: Harberger-taxed identity berths stop sybil farms at the wharf. A newcomer claims one berth, sets its own price, and locks a cipher lease proving sole control. Second, it pays 2% of the stated price daily as tax, and anyone may buy the berth at that price, so hoarding invites a buyout. Third, peers audit leases weekly; proven duplicates forfeit the deposit and lose the berth. Holding 1,000 fake berths at $40 each locks $40,000 and burns $800 a day in tax. Like shale laid down by a patient river, a berth stays honest only while its owner keeps paying to hold it.
